C-SUBSTANCE-OVER-NAME.Summary: Close F35 and the two items it dragged with it: one structural-clone definition in `src/` verified by **body** rather than by identifier (`cloneNode` at `gates/ledger.ts:165` survived a criterion that counted the name `cloneXmlNode`); `appendEpochToLedger`'s inlined one-level copy replaced by the shared helper; and the preserved-evidence digest check made to name its own failure cause (F36's owed half). Takes the P0 open count from one to zero.
C-SUBSTANCE-OVER-NAME.Problem:
**Shared shape.** Three sites where a check or a copy is bound to a **name** instead of to the **thing the name means**, so the binding holds while the meaning drifts.
| item | what it says | what it is bound to | | F35 | one structural clone in the codebase | occurrences of one identifier | | residual | clone the ledger tree | an inline literal that copies one level | | F36 owed | these bytes are preserved | a digest, with no statement of the length |
---
**F35 — the criterion counted an identifier.** `C-CONTRACT-DEBT` `AC-CLONE-XML-SINGLE-HOME` states its post-condition as
``` rg -n 'function cloneXmlNode' src/ → exactly one definition, in xml.ts ```
That is true at `74ef83d` and the duplication it exists to remove is not gone. Measured at this authoring HEAD:
``` rg -n 'cloneNode' src/ → src/gates/ledger.ts:165 function cloneNode(node: GraceXmlNode): GraceXmlNode { → src/gates/ledger.ts:169 children: node.children.map(cloneNode), → src/gates/ledger.ts:192 return cloneNode(artifact.root); ```
Same algorithm — tag, `{ ...attributes }`, recursive children, text — differing from the exported `cloneXmlNode` only by the six characters the shorter identifier saves (196 bytes against 202). The spec's own survey could not have found it: it ranged over a **name** while the claim was about a **body**.
`gates/ledger.ts` already imports `readGraceXmlArtifact` and the `GraceXmlNode` type from `../artifact/xml`, so the repair is one import token and a deletion. It was out of `C-CONTRACT-DEBT`'s approved `ObservedWriteScope` — the same constraint that produced F20 — which is why it is here rather than folded in.
**The repair owes a check that would have caught it.** A post-condition re-stated as "one occurrence of `cloneNode` too" is the same defect with a longer list. The check must be able to fail on a copy nobody has named yet.
---
**Residual — `appendEpochToLedger` inlines a shallower copy.** `src/grace-cursor.ts:2871` builds the ledger root by hand:
```ts children: existing.root.children.map((child) => ({ tag: child.tag, attributes: { ...child.attributes }, children: [...child.children], // grandchild nodes shared text: child.text, })), ```
Its sibling at `:2271` clones the same shape with the deep helper.
**Stated honestly, because it changes what may be claimed:** this is a latent hazard, **not** an observable defect. The shared level is never mutated — the array is freshly allocated, and `existing` is discarded after the write — so **no behavioural test discriminates the fixed version from the current one.** The repair removes a trap for the next writer who mutates that tree; the assertion that it landed is structural, and this spec requires it to be declared as structural rather than dressed as behavioural.
---
**F36 owed half — the digest failure could not name its cause.** `src/grace-status.test.ts:697` pins the live `NaN` orphan's SHA-1. When a CRLF checkout moved those bytes, the failure printed two hex strings and nothing else; diagnosis took a byte-level comparison. The file carries exactly one newline: **135** bytes as LF, **136** as CRLF. Asserting the length beside the digest turns the next occurrence into a one-line read. The root cause is already fixed (`.gitattributes`, `9badb10`); this is the legibility half, deferred then because it is a `src/` edit and an ungoverned `src/` change is this repository's stated failure mode.

Goals.Goal: **F35.** `src/gates/ledger.ts` holds no local structural clone; it imports `cloneXmlNode` from `../artifact/xml`. After the change exactly **one** structural-clone definition exists in `src/`, and that fact is pinned by a check that compares **function bodies**, so a copy under any new identifier fails it.

**Residual.** `appendEpochToLedger` uses the shared helper instead of an inline one-level copy, so both ledger-tree paths in `grace-cursor.ts` clone by the same definition. Declared as a structural repair with no behavioural discriminator.

**F36 owed.** The preserved-evidence check asserts the orphan's byte length before its digest, so a line-ending conversion reports a length mismatch that names the cause instead of an opaque hex mismatch.

**P0.** With F35 closed, `RM-GOVERNED-PATH` P0's open-finding count reaches zero and the phase may move `EXECUTING → COMPLETE`, which is the gate on the 6.2.0 release. The board update is the authority's act, not a task here.

Constraints.Constraint: Binding: decisions.md F35, F35.1, F36, F20, F23, F10 (a name claiming more than the body verifies), F26 (`at close` on lint), F27/F27.2 (`ObservedWriteScope` covers what the deliverable **forces**), F33 (criteria do not freeze counts measured at authoring), F4 (this pass is **spec only**, `status="draft"`; no `plan.xml` until approved).

**Decided here, not deferred to the plan.** The plan may choose the scan's mechanism, its home, and test layout, but must not re-open: clone semantics stay exactly as `cloneXmlNode` implements them today; the single home stays `src/artifact/xml.ts`; the single-definition check is **body-shaped**, never a list of known identifiers; the `appendEpochToLedger` repair is declared structural; the orphan's pinned SHA-1 value is not changed.
Ceremony tier **T1** — single subject, three small surfaces, no cross-cutting protocol change and no new public API.

AffectedAreas is closed and binds the plan. Anticipated write surface: `src/gates/ledger.ts` (delete local clone; import), `src/grace-cursor.ts` (residual), `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` (body-shaped single-definition check), `src/grace-status.test.ts` (length assertion), `src/gates/core.test.ts` (only if the ledger change forces coverage there — it already imports from `./ledger`). **Stop and re-spec** rather than expanding into skills, review catalog, graph, or version surfaces.

**Do not edit** `docs/plans/**` (including decisions.md), `.ngrace/changes/archive/**`, CHANGELOG.md, `.gitattributes`, or any version surface. Packaged version at authoring: **6.1.1**. No product version bump — 6.2.0 is a separate release act gated on P0.

Evidence doctrine: red-first per AC, each red in its own tool round trip before the production edit. Exact pins (F23). Mutation probes: rename a clone copy and confirm the scan still fails; delete the length assertion and confirm a CRLF fixture no longer names its cause; restore the inline one-level copy and confirm the structural assertion fails.

NonGoals.NonGoal: **Rejected — re-state the post-condition as "no `cloneNode` either".** A longer list of identifiers is F35 with more rows.
**Rejected — a behavioural test for the `appendEpochToLedger` repair.** None discriminates; claiming one would be the defect this bundle is about. Declared structural instead.
**Rejected — changing `cloneXmlNode`'s semantics**, exporting it from a second module, or generalising it (deep-freeze, structuredClone). This is a move and a deletion.

De-duplicating any other helper family; a repo-wide duplicate-code detector; changing the orphan's pinned digest; editing `.gitattributes`; F37's disposition (recorded as authoring guidance by the authority, not implemented here).
Any product version bump, CHANGELOG edit, or P0 board edit.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CLONE-ONE-DEFINITION-BY-BODY: A check in the suite proves that `src/` contains exactly **one** structural-clone-over-`GraceXmlNode` definition and that it is the export in `src/artifact/xml.ts`. The check compares **normalized function bodies** — identifier-insensitive, so a copy named anything fails it. Discrimination is proven, not asserted: adding a copy under a fresh name (for example `duplicateNode`) reddens the check, and the probe output is recorded verbatim. **Failure conditions:** the check greps for `cloneXmlNode` or any fixed list of names; a renamed copy passes; the scan enumerates known files rather than scanning `src/`; the check asserts a count without asserting the surviving definition's location.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-LEDGER-IMPORTS-SHARED-CLONE: `src/gates/ledger.ts` contains no local structural-clone function and imports `cloneXmlNode` from `../artifact/xml`. `loadOrCreateLedgerRoot` returns a tree with the same semantics as before (deep structural clone of the parsed root). `M-GATES`' MODULE_CONTRACT and MODULE_MAP stay true — the helper was private, so `MAP_MODE: EXPORTS` parity does not change, and the map must **not** gain `cloneXmlNode`. Existing gate behaviour is unchanged: `bun test src/gates/core.test.ts` green. **Failure conditions:** map gains an imported symbol; ledger re-exports the helper; `SCOPE` rewritten to accommodate it; clone semantics altered at this call site.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-APPEND-EPOCH-USES-ONE-DEFINITION: `appendEpochToLedger` (`src/grace-cursor.ts`) no longer builds children with an inline one-level copy; it clones through the shared helper, so both ledger-tree paths in that file use one definition. **This criterion is structural and must be declared as such** — the plan and the executor state plainly that no behavioural test discriminates, because the shared level is never mutated. A `TargetAssertion` over the source is the honest pin. Fold behaviour is unchanged: the cursor suite stays green and a fold still round-trips. **Failure conditions:** a test is written that claims to prove isolation but would pass on the pre-change code; the criterion is reported as behaviourally verified; fold output changes.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DIGEST-FAILURE-NAMES-ITS-CAUSE: The preserved-evidence check at `src/grace-status.test.ts` asserts the orphan's **byte length** before its SHA-1, with an exact `toBe` of the re-measured length (authoring HEAD: **135** — F33: implementation re-measures, the criterion does not freeze it). The pinned SHA-1 value is unchanged. Proven discriminating: against a CRLF copy of the same content the length assertion fails **first** and names 136 against 135. **Failure conditions:** length asserted after the digest, so the digest still fails first; a range or `toBeGreaterThan`; the SHA-1 pin weakened, normalized, or removed; the probe not run.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-HEAD-RED: Each criterion above has a red recorded **before** its production edit, in its own tool round trip, with the failing test written first so the fail event's `WriteEvidence` carries it (never a red backed only by a grep, and never a retrospective red via stash). At authoring HEAD the reds are available: the body-shaped scan does not exist; `gates/ledger.ts:165` defines `cloneNode`; `grace-cursor.ts:2871` inlines the one-level copy; the length assertion is absent. **Failure conditions:** a check that passes on pre-change HEAD while claiming to prove the new property; fail and pass attempts recorded in one tool call.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-AND-LINT: `bun test` green; `bun run validate:ci` green with the determinism ratchet cardinality unchanged (authoring HEAD: **14** caught keys — re-measure, do not adjust); `bun run ngrace lint --path .` is 0 errors and 0 warnings **at close** (after apply and archive — not claimed mid-change, where the plan's own `BaselineAssertions` are expected red). `ObservedWriteScope` covers every path the deliverable forces. **Failure conditions:** suite red; lint 0/0 claimed mid-window; ratchet keys dropped to keep a number; writes outside declared scope.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-ARCHIVE-OR-ROADMAP-EDITS: No writes under `docs/plans/**`, `.ngrace/changes/archive/**`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `.gitattributes`, or any version surface (stays 6.1.1). **Failure conditions:** the P0 board edited from inside the bundle; the orphan file itself edited to make a digest agree.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Integration (T1): exactly one structural-clone body in `src/`, located in `artifact/xml.ts`, proven by an identifier-insensitive scan whose discrimination probe (a copy under a fresh name) is recorded verbatim; `gates/ledger.ts` importing rather than defining, with `M-GATES` map unchanged; `appendEpochToLedger` cloning through the shared helper with the structural-only nature of that claim stated; the orphan length assertion failing first against a CRLF fixture; lint 0/0 **at close** only; validate:ci green with ratchet keys preserved.

Assumptions.Assumption:
**F35 survey at authoring HEAD `74ef83d`:**
``` rg -n 'function cloneXmlNode' src/ → src/artifact/xml.ts:161 (exported) rg -n 'cloneNode' src/ → src/gates/ledger.ts:165, :169, :192 ```
Bodies identical apart from the identifier; 196 bytes against 202. `gates/ledger.ts` already imports `readGraceXmlArtifact` and the `GraceXmlNode` type from `../artifact/xml`. `cloneNode` is private, so `MAP_MODE: EXPORTS` parity on `M-GATES` does not change.

**Test homes measured, not assumed:** `src/gates/core.test.ts` already imports from `./ledger` (line 29), so ledger coverage has an existing home and no new test file is forced. `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` owns `cloneXmlNode`'s behavioural coverage from `C-CONTRACT-DEBT` T-002 and is the natural home for the single-definition scan. `src/docs-claims.test.ts` is the precedent for a test that reads repository files and asserts a claim about them.

**Residual site:** `src/grace-cursor.ts:2871` — inline copy with `children: [...child.children]`, sharing grandchild node objects; the sibling deep clone is at `:2271`. No caller mutates the shared level, which is why the repair has no behavioural discriminator.

**F36 subject:** `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY/run/NaN-T-001-opened.xml` — 135 bytes, one newline, SHA-1 `c0cc8899…` as LF; 136 bytes and `bab374c4…` as CRLF. Root cause fixed at `9badb10` (`.gitattributes`, `* text=auto eol=lf`); this bundle adds only the length assertion.

Counts at authoring HEAD: lint 0 errors / 0 warnings; determinism ratchet 14 caught keys; archive holds 29 bundles; `active/` is empty before this bundle. F33: implementation re-measures all of these.
